transcript.text:
Thank you all. Let me take stock of where we stand before I make my decision. On the record, I now have findings from all four consulted functions:

1. Loan Operations (Nadia): The servicing platform can enforce a weekly borrowing-base certificate, the risk team requires it weekly, and the operating instruction must be added to the draft closing checklist before closing.

2. Credit Risk (Ravi): Revised downside analysis supports approval only with a 6-month extension, exactly $1,000,000 principal paydown, and an 850-basis-point cash interest rate. The written analysis has not yet been attached to the underwriting file and must be before closing.

3. Banking Counsel (Marta): Three intercreditor closing-package items required — equipment lender's written consent before any maturity extension, amended-loan prohibition on additional liens on production equipment, and a separate intercreditor-consent commitment recorded in the closing package. All must be satisfied before closing.

4. Relationship Management (Jonah): Borrower owners will fund exactly $750,000 of new cash at restructuring close. This has been recorded in coverage notes but not yet updated in the credit file.

On the two independent terms: principal paydown is $1,000,000 per credit risk, and borrower cash injection is $750,000 per relationship management. These are distinct and separately specified.

Before I settle, I want to note the outstanding pre-closing items that will be reflected as commitments in the approval memo: (a) Ravi's written analysis must be attached to the underwriting file, (b) the weekly borrowing-base certificate operating instruction must be added to the closing checklist, (c) the equipment lender's written consent must be obtained, (d) the amended-loan prohibition on additional liens must be included, (e) the intercreditor-consent commitment must be recorded, (f) Jonah must update the credit file with the borrower cash injection confirmation, and (g) Marta's legal note should be circulated. I will now settle the restructuring package.
